title: Stationary inert-active factorization and orthogonality in symmetric operadic families
statement: Use small quasicategories and their mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], symmetric operadic families of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $S$ be a small quasicategory and let $\pi:M^\otimes\to S\times N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ be an $S$-family of symmetric infinity-operads. Call an edge stationary inert if it is $\pi$-cocartesian, its $S$-edge is an identity, and its pointed map is inert; call an edge active if its pointed map is active, with no restriction on its $S$-edge. Every edge $h:x\to z$ admits a factorization $x\xrightarrow{i}x_D\xrightarrow{a}z$ with $i$ stationary inert and $a$ active. If $\alpha:\langle k\rangle\to\langle l\rangle$ is the pointed map of $h$, then $D=\{u\ne *:\alpha(u)\ne *\}$, $x_D$ is the inert restriction over $D_+=D\amalg\{*\}$ in the parameter fiber of $x$, and the factorization includes a specified composition homotopy to $h$. For any stationary inert $i:x\to y$ and any active $a:u\to v$, the composition map $$\operatorname{Map}_{M^\otimes}(y,u)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{M^\otimes}(x,u)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{M^\otimes}(x,v)}\operatorname{Map}_{M^\otimes}(y,v),\quad f\longmapsto(fi,af)$$ is an equivalence, natural in the square data. The homotopy pullback records a path between the two composites, and the assertion includes all higher homotopies and empty retained-input sets. No categorical or operadic structure on the total family over $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ alone is assumed.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp.336-337; relative cocartesian factorization and blockwise Segal comparison.

proof.text: Let $h:x\to z$ lie over $(\sigma,\alpha)$, with $\alpha:\langle k\rangle\to\langle l\rangle$. Put $D=\{u\ne *:\alpha(u)\ne *\}$ and $D_+=D\amalg\{*\}$. Define $r:\langle k\rangle\to D_+$ to fix $D$ and send all other inputs to $*$; define $s:D_+\to\langle l\rangle$ to agree with $\alpha$ on $D$. Each non-basepoint of $D_+$ has exactly one preimage under $r$, and only $*$ maps to $*$ under $s$. Thus $r$ is inert, $s$ is active, and $sr=\alpha$, by the pointed-map definitions in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction].

source.place: Higher Algebra, Remark 2.1.2.2 and Proposition 2.1.2.5, printed pp.178-179; relative version supporting Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof step (1), printed pp.336-337

proof.text: The family condition supplies a $\pi$-cocartesian lift $i:x\to x_D$ of $(1,r)$ within the parameter fiber of $x$. Its parameter edge is an identity, so it is stationary inert. In $S\times N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ take the $2$-simplex whose $S$-coordinate is the degeneracy of $\sigma$ with repeated source and whose pointed-set edges are $r,s,\alpha=sr$. Its edges $01$ and $02$ lift to $i$ and $h$, respectively, defining a horn $\Lambda^2_0$. The cocartesian outer-horn condition in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] fills this horn over that base simplex. The remaining edge is $a:x_D\to z$ over $(\sigma,s)$, and the filler is the specified composition triangle from $ai$ to $h$. By the definition of the active subcategory in [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], $a$ is active.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Remark 2.1.2.2 and Proposition 2.1.2.5, printed pp.178-179; relative version supporting Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof step (1), printed pp.336-337

proof.text: For the orthogonality assertion fix $i:x\to y$ stationary inert and $a:u\to v$ active. Write $\bar i:I\to J$ and $\bar a:U\to V$ for their pointed maps. Given pointed maps $b:I\to U$ and $c:J\to V$ with $\bar a b=c\bar i$, define $t(*)=*$ and $t(j)=b(d_j)$ for $j\ne *$, where $d_j$ is the unique preimage of $j$ under $\bar i$. This gives $\bar a t=c$. If $\bar i(d)=*$, the square equation gives $\bar a b(d)=*$, hence $b(d)=*$ by activity. Thus $t\bar i=b$, and these equations determine $t$ uniquely. This proves the Hom-set pullback directly from the pointed-map definitions. The right-pinched mapping space of an ordinary nerve is the constant simplicial set on its Hom set: the initial face is constant, and a functor $[n+1]\to C$ with that face is determined by its last edge. Hence this is also the mapping-space homotopy pullback in $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$. Set $B=S\times N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$. Its mapping spaces are products degreewise. The analogous square in $S$ has identity horizontal maps since $\pi_S(i)$ is an identity. Pairing the inverse of that identity-square comparison with the pointed-set inverse $t$ gives the base homotopy-pullback square for $\pi(i),\pi(a)$; the path-space formula is coordinatewise in a product.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Remark 2.1.2.2 and Proposition 2.1.2.5, printed pp.178-179; relative version supporting Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof step (1), printed pp.336-337

proof.text:
Write $M(p,q)=\operatorname{Map}_{M^\otimes}(p,q)$ and $B(p,q)=\operatorname{Map}_{B}(\pi p,\pi q)$. The family projection is a categorical fibration. By [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] it lifts inner horns, since these are trivial cofibrations; hence it is an inner fibration. Thus so the cocartesian mapping criterion applied to $i$ with targets $u$ and $v$ gives $M(y,w)\simeq M(x,w)\times^h_{B(x,w)}B(y,w)$ for $w=u,v$. The base square proved in Step 3 gives $B(y,u)\simeq B(x,u)\times^h_{B(x,v)}B(y,v)$. Pasting these pullbacks, with the specified commutation homotopies, gives
$$M(y,u)\simeq M(x,u)\times^h_{B(x,v)}B(y,v).$$
On the other hand the target of the asserted comparison is
$$M(x,u)\times^h_{M(x,v)}M(y,v)\simeq M(x,u)\times^h_{M(x,v)}\bigl(M(x,v)\times^h_{B(x,v)}B(y,v)\bigr)\simeq M(x,u)\times^h_{B(x,v)}B(y,v).$$
These are exactly the two applications of homotopy-pullback pasting/cancellation, so the square induced by precomposition with $i$ and postcomposition with $a$ is a homotopy pullback.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Remark 2.1.2.2 and Proposition 2.1.2.5, printed pp.178-179; relative version supporting Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof step (1), printed pp.336-337

proof.text: The comparison of this square takes $f:y\to u$ to $(fi,af)$ and the associativity homotopy between $a(fi)$ and $(af)i$. This path comes from composition for the triple $(i,f,a)$, not from the unrelated factorization triangle of Step 2. The face and degeneracy coherence in [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] supplies that homotopy in all simplicial degrees, naturally in functors and square data; [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] identifies its precomposition and postcomposition maps with the right-pinched mapping-space convention used here. The specified-homotopy clause of [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] identifies the comparisons in Step 4 using precisely these paths. Consequently Step 4 proves that the displayed composition comparison itself is an equivalence of spaces, retaining every higher simplex, and the comparison is natural.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Remark 2.1.2.2 and Proposition 2.1.2.5, printed pp.178-179; relative version supporting Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof step (1), printed pp.336-337

proof.text: When $D=\varnothing$, $r$ is the unique map to $\langle0\rangle$ and $s$ is the unique pointed map from it, which is active. If $l=0$, then necessarily $D=\varnothing$. The family axiom supplies the same inert lift and the same horn argument applies. In Step 3 an empty $J\setminus\{*\}$ leaves only $t(*)=*$; the square equation and activity still force $b$ to be the constant basepoint map. Thus the mapping pullback calculation also applies at zero arity. All empty products have the point value specified in the family definition.
